name: Sign in and open the controller dashboard
description: Verifies the main entry page leads to sign-in and the supplied demo credentials open the controller dashboard.
steps: Open the homepage
Open Sign in
Enter username user and password user123
Submit the form
expected: The dashboard opens and shows the VoiceHome Controller, voice command area, connected spaces, and system status cards.

name: Add a room and map it to an available GPIO
description: Verifies a user can add a new room through the web interface and map it to a free ESP8266 GPIO pin.
setup: Sign in as user with password user123
steps: Open Spaces & GPIO
Click Add space
Enter Study Room and Study Room Bulb
Select D1
Enter study room, office as voice aliases
Submit the form
expected: Study Room appears in the room mapping with Study Room Bulb, GPIO D1, and the configured voice aliases.

name: Control a configured room manually
description: Verifies a manual toggle queues a command in the database and the switch flips once the controller acknowledges it.
setup: Sign in as user with password user123
steps: Open the dashboard
Toggle the Sitting Room Bulb switch
Wait for the status line to show the queued message
Wait up to 8 seconds (3s device poll + 5s dashboard refresh)
expected: The status line shows 'queued — waiting for controller', the voice log lists the manual command as queued, and the switch flips to the new ON or OFF state after the controller acknowledges the command (requires the ESP8266 online or a simulated heartbeat ack).

name: Reject invalid login
description: Verifies incorrect credentials do not open the smart home dashboard.
steps: Open the sign-in page
Enter username wrong and password wrong
Submit the form
expected: An invalid username or password message is shown and the dashboard is not opened.

name: Pending command expires if not claimed within 15 seconds
description: Verifies a command that no controller claims within the 15 second claim deadline is marked expired and can never execute.
setup: Sign in as user with password user123
Ensure the ESP8266 is offline (or no controller polls the endpoint)
steps: Toggle a device to queue a pending command
Record its id from the voice log
Wait at least 16 seconds
Query the command status via GET /api/commands
expected: The command status is 'expired' after the claim deadline and is not returned to any controller as a command to execute.

name: Claimed command expires if not acknowledged within 25 seconds
description: Verifies a command that was claimed but never acknowledged within the 25 second execution deadline is expired, and a late acknowledgement cannot revive it or mark it executed.
setup: Sign in as user with password user123
Have a controller claim a command but withhold the acknowledgement
steps: Queue a command and let a controller claim it (status 'claimed')
Do not send an acknowledgement
Wait more than 25 seconds from creation
Send a late acknowledgement for the same command id
expected: The command status is 'expired'; the late acknowledgement returns { ok: false, status: 'expired' } and the command is not marked executed.

name: Expiry sweeps are idempotent and report correct counts
description: Verifies running the shared expiry helper repeatedly does not re-expire already terminal rows and returns zero affected rows once everything is expired.
setup: Two commands older than their deadlines exist as pending/claimed
steps: Call the expiry sweep once
Call the expiry sweep again
Compare affected-row counts
expected: The first sweep changes only the eligible stale rows; the second sweep changes zero rows.

name: Cancel a pending command immediately
description: Verifies a pending command can be cancelled via the authenticated cancel endpoint and the dashboard reflects the cancelled state.
setup: Sign in as user with password user123
steps: Click Cancel on the pending command in the voice log
Observe the status line and the command row
expected: POST /api/commands/{id}/cancel/ returns { ok: true, status: 'cancelled' }, the row shows 'cancelled', and the controller never receives the command.

name: Cancellation is safe against terminal states and late acknowledgements
description: Verifies that repeated cancellation, cancelling an executed command, and a late acknowledgement cannot overwrite a terminal state.
steps: Cancel a pending command
Call cancel again for the same command
Attempt to cancel an executed command
Send a late acknowledgement for the cancelled command
expected: The second cancel does not change state and returns the actual status; executed commands are not overwritten; the late acknowledgement cannot revive the cancelled command.

name: Cancelling a claimed command reports that the action may have occurred
description: Verifies a claimed command cannot be silently cancelled and the API explains that the physical action cannot be guaranteed to be prevented.
setup: Have a controller claim a command
steps: Call POST /api/commands/{id}/cancel/ for the claimed command
expected: The endpoint returns HTTP 409 with the actual status 'claimed' and a message stating the physical action cannot be guaranteed to be prevented.

name: Refreshing the dashboard does not resubmit or execute old commands
description: Verifies that reloading the dashboard never creates a new command and that old pending commands are expired rather than re-executed.
setup: Leave it unclaimed past the claim deadline
steps: Reload the dashboard several times
Observe the voice log and the network requests
expected: No new command is POSTed on mount, the old command shows 'expired', and no command is executed as a result of the reload.

name: Reset data clears commands and restores default rooms
description: Verifies the Reset data action clears commands and reseeds the default devices/rooms without executing anything.
setup: Sign in as user with password user123
steps: Queue at least one command
Click Reset data and confirm
Reload the dashboard
expected: The voice log is empty, the four default rooms/devices are restored, and no command was executed by the reset.

name: Five-second refresh runs only while active commands exist
description: Verifies the dashboard polls approximately every five seconds only while at least one pending or claimed command exists, and stops otherwise.
setup: Sign in as user with password user123
steps: Queue a pending command
Observe GET /api/commands requests over ten seconds
Cancel or resolve the command
Observe requests over another ten seconds
expected: Requests occur roughly every five seconds while an active command exists and stop once no pending/claimed commands remain; no overlapping refresh requests are issued.

name: Concurrent controller polls cannot claim the same command twice
description: Verifies that two concurrent poll requests result in exactly one claim of a single pending command.
steps: Queue one pending command
Issue two controller poll requests concurrently
Inspect how many responses include the command
expected: Exactly one poll response contains the command; the other returns { command: null }, and the command is executed at most once.
